statements.t: For example, our expectations regarding certain items as a percentage of sales assume that we will achieve our anticipated sales goals.

We expect that we will continue our product manufacturing activities in order to generate a targeted amount of inventory of maritime satellite connectivity and satellite television terminals to meet anticipated demand and that we will cease substantially all manufacturing activity by the end of 2026.
We expect to continue to facilitate customer transition to third-party hardware products compatible with our mobile satellite communications services.
We also plan to continue to conduct maintenance, service, warehousing, shipping and receiving activities at our Bristol, Rhode Island location.
During the third quarter of 2024, we commenced our plan to sell the warehouse building and surface parking lot located at 75 Enterprise Center in Middletown, Rhode Island (“75 Enterprise Center”).

Additionally, in the third quarter of 2024, we commenced our plan to sell the property, building, improvements, and land located at 50 Enterprise Center in Middletown, Rhode Island (“50 Enterprise Center”).
The Company did not record comparable gains and losses from property dispositions and project write-offs during the nine months ended September 30, 2026.
These asset sales were non-recurring, and we do not expect comparable proceeds to be available in future periods.

Based upon our current working capital position, current operating plans and expected business conditions, we expect to have sufficient funds through at least twelve months from the date that this report is filed with the SEC to fund our short-term and long-term working capital requirements, including capital expenditures, contractual obligations and potential acquisitions.
We expect that any such agreement would take effect on December 1, 2026.

Starlink has recently implemented price increases across its Starlink service offerings, including those available to resellers such as KVH, and we anticipate that price increases will be reflected in the terms of any new arrangement.

Our negotiation with Starlink is ongoing and we can make no assurances regarding the terms on which Starlink data (including data under our existing agreement) will be available to us, the timeline to reach a definitive agreement, or whether a definitive agreement will be reached at all.
Our funding plans for our working capital needs and other commitments may be adversely impacted if our underlying assumptions regarding our anticipated revenues and expenses are not realized.

Because of these limitations, there can be no assurance that any system of disclosure controls and procedures or internal control over financial reporting will be successful in preventing all errors or fraud or in making all material information known in a timely manner to the appropriate levels of management.
We anticipate that, as a result of recent Starlink price increases, the terms of any new arrangement will be less favorable than the terms of our existing arrangement and include price increases.

Alternative LEO capacity, such as Eutelsat OneWeb, may not be available in sufficient quantities, on comparable terms, or with the performance characteristics our customers expect, and switching customers to an alternative service would be costly and time-consuming and could result in customer losses.

There can be no assurance that we will enter into a new arrangement on acceptable terms or at all, and if we do not, our revenue, profitability and cash flows will be materially and adversely affected.
The mobile connectivity market is intensely competitive, and we expect the intensity of competition to continue to increase in the future.
